title: Fetch TESS QLP/TESScut, ZTF and ASAS-SN live for LC vetting, with matched detrending and retried/paged ZTF queries
what_happened: The sole Tier C survivor 5628404318169472 carried two not_evaluated holes that code could close. pipeline_agreement never received a second TESS extraction because live enrichment fetched no TESS data, and the adversarial review's hand comparison of QLP vs. TESScut (raw r = 0.43-0.81) used different detrending on each series. second_survey never received ZTF or ASAS-SN because live enrichment had no optical survey fetch, and the reviewer's own IRSA ZTF cone requests timed out at 40 s unless narrowed to one band list and a 6 arcsec cone.
generic_lesson: A cross-pipeline comparison is only meaningful when both series go through the identical detrending filter at matched cadences, using the detection channel's own window. Archive time-series queries that can time out need bounded retries, a shrinking cone and time-window paging, and every failure mode must surface in the check note instead of silently reading as no coverage. Vetting-only time series are stored apart from channel inputs so new vetting data never changes a certified channel score.
